title: Flywheel scenario
description: One scenario as data (94): given this evidence, when these ticks, responses and events, then these transitions, effects and decisions. Every scenario states the requirements it satisfies by number. Every vocabulary here is closed, so a typo fails validation rather than being ignored.

profiles.description: the state store bindings this scenario runs on, and nothing else; the recorded-versus-real axis is `requires`

requires.description: what the run must provide beyond the store binding (93a). `real-workspace`: the scenario asserts a real take, merge, rebase, conflict or landing, so the recorded workspace stand-in cannot serve it. `real-sessions`: it asserts a real agent session rather than a scripted one. A run whose bound implementations do not provide a requirement skips the scenario, prints it as skipped with the reason, and names it in the run record; a scenario the phase's acceptance table lists but every configuration skips is a failure, never a silent pass.

hooks.description: in-process fault injection the runner honours only when it holds the engine itself, which is the mode without `--hosts real`. Allowed only under `contract/`: these force a race the machinery is built to prevent, so they prove the guarantee rather than exercise the domain. `bypass_lease`: the acting hosts attempt their writes without taking the lease first (B.2.134). `interrupt_write`: the acting host's write is cut off midway (B.2.135).

invariants.description: invariants of section 7 the scenario checks

machines.description: machines directory to load; default ../machines; contract scenarios use ./contract/lamp

register.description: the rail's decision register: decision id -> number, and the counter

state_store.description: assertions on the profile's own behaviour (rejections, ids, as-of). Every key is bound in `observations.yaml`, which names its meaning and the profiles that answer it; `machines/check.py` fails a key that file does not bind, so an invented key can no longer pass silently.

evidence.description: evidence name -> {object id -> value}; '*' for every object

files.description: what the world reports on disk, as path -> content or path -> a description of the content. Every path is resolved against `conformance/fixtures/`; a path that names a file there is materialized into the scenario's temporary checkout, and a value that is not a fixture path is taken as inline content for it. A path resolving to no fixture and to no inline content is invalid (exit 2).

script.description: what the stand-in session binding plays, per session id (93): the exits and offers a real session would report through the command, and the pane and activity the multiplexer would show. Only the session binding is faked; every other binding is real.

after.description: the step number to play at, counting from 0. A script entry never carries a duration: the clock moves only through a `clock` step and the tick interval, so a delay is written as a `clock` step in `when`.

keystroke.description: the operator typed in the pane

service.description: the session runs `flywheel service start|stop <name>` on its bolt's declared service (48): {start: <name>} or {stop: <name>}

commits.description: files the session commits in its place

concurrent_hosts.description: these hosts tick at the same moment against the same store, which is how a race is written. Without it the tick runs as the acting host alone.

interval.description: how far this tick moves the virtual clock; the run's declared interval otherwise, which defaults to the profile's sweep.

run.description: run the named scenario file to completion in place of ticking this one, which is how a scenario asserts that the scenario tool runs a scenario (95).

decision.description: <object id>/<decision kind>, resolved through the register at the moment the step runs; a scenario naming no standing decision fails

number.description: the number the register gave, for answering the same decision again (15)

object.description: for a dictation: the object it names

host.description: the following steps run as this host until the next host step, and at most one transition is performed on it. `name: none` means no host is acting.

start.description: a host that was not running joins and starts fresh

lose.description: the host is lost without warning: no shutdown, no release

disconnect.description: the host keeps running and cannot reach the state store

return.description: a lost or disconnected host comes back

advance.description: how far the virtual clock moves: 30s, 6m, 1d. With the tick interval this is the only thing that moves time; real wall-clock time never reaches a guard.

at.description: the time of day the clock lands on after advancing, for a cadence a scenario must hit exactly

script.description: seed or extend the stand-in's script mid-scenario

direct.description: something acts outside the machinery's own loop and the machinery must read it as it finds it. `do` names which, and each arm carries its own fields, so a misspelled key fails validation.

by.description: the identity that acted; the operator unless stated

text.description: what the operator said in chat; the host's agent proposes the tool call and the operator's confirmation is the response (194)

command.description: the adapter's own binary writing a capture, from any machine (217g); a path in it resolves against `fixtures/`

path.description: the page route the operator opened

command.description: the operator ran this by hand, outside every tool (S15, X08)
